PullRequest.Title: Handle indexed search telemetry in Agent Host
PullRequest.Body:

Logs `session.indexed_search` as an intentionally handled Copilot SDK event while excluding potentially sensitive error details.

Adds GDPR declarations for the indexed-search telemetry already forwarded by the Copilot runtime, including per-search `search_engine` attribution.

Validation:
- Passed targeted unit tests for `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` and `copilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder.test.ts` (627 tests).
- Passed telemetry extraction for `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot`.
- Passed pre-commit hygiene checks for all 5 changed files.
- Completed a focused code review with no actionable findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot indexed-search lifecycle events during repository startup, incremental indexing, and server failure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK event dispatch synchronously reaches the session wrapper and trace logging callback. Before the PR the same event synchronously reached the unhandled-event trace callback; after the PR it is classified as handled and logs only event data with startup/server error details removed. No indexing work waits on any newly introduced subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Trace-log emission through ILogService when trace logging is enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trace call per session.indexed_search event; lifecycle events are aggregate startup, incremental-update, or server-error notifications rather than per-file logging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic onUnhandledEvent callback already called safeStringify on the entire indexed-search event and issued one trace log. The PR marks the type handled and serializes a smaller data object, omitting envelope fields and potentially large error text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous payload copying/stringification occurs during event dispatch; downstream trace output may write to a logger, but the PR does not add an extra log call for the event.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of aggregate indexed-search lifecycle notifications over a session, not repository file count; payload measurements summarize file counts and changes. Startup/server-error payload copying is bounded by the event fields and excludes errorMessage.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous listener callback per indexed-search event per active SDK session; no new queue, limiter, parallel fan-out, or coalescing behavior. The dedicated typed SDK listener replaces unhandled processing for this event type rather than running alongside it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or lookup state is added. Listener creation is lazy on first access and lives with the disposable session, matching existing wrapper event ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the wrapper handled-event set, listener registration order, and pre-existing unhandled trace callback that the new typed path replaces rather than duplicates event logging.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact indexed-search event frequency and trace logger implementation vary by runtime and log level, but the diff reduces serialized content relative to the existing path and does not increase boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one pre-existing trace serialization/log operation remains one operation per event, with less data and sensitive error text removed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Forwarding Copilot indexed-search and grep search-engine telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The connection-global onGitHubTelemetry callback routes each notification through the existing CopilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder, which constructs telemetry data and calls ITelemetryService.publicLog. The changed production lines are GDPR declaration comments only, so no runtime work or boundary is added or moved onto the path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing publicLog call per accepted SDK telemetry notification; restricted server-error telemetry is dropped when restricted telemetry is disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic forwarder already spread all event properties and metrics, including search_engine and tgrep event fields, and invoked publicLog for every accepted event kind. The PR only declares those already-forwarded fields for telemetry extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the user interaction/indexing critical path beyond existing notification handling; declarations do not create or increase delivery calls.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of SDK telemetry notifications; indexed-search notifications are aggregate events, and the change does not alter their production, grouping, or effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing callback behavior is unchanged: one routing/forwarding operation per SDK telemetry notification, with restricted notifications gated by policy and response-only correlation logic unaffected. No changed batching, limiter, serialization, or fan-out behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Restricted telemetry policy lookup and existing routing behavior remain unchanged; there is no new positive, negative, or coalescing cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the diff and forwarder implementation: declarations are comments consumed by build-time extraction, while runtime forwarding already generically included arbitrary properties and metrics.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual telemetry transport latency is implementation-dependent, but no changed executable code reaches that boundary, making regression magnitude effectively zero.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: runtime telemetry boundary count, payload construction, concurrency, and critical-path placement are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff hunks. The only executable product change replaces existing unhandled-event trace serialization with a smaller typed payload; telemetry additions are non-executable declarations, and tests add no shipped runtime cost. No actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
